newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says policy aims at strengthening recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says policy aims at strengthening recovery.

text.p: The monetary policy of the Bank of Japan (BOJ) continues to aim at strengthening the basis for economic recovery, BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Thursday.

"In managing our current monetary policy, it is appropriate to carefully watch developments (in the economy and prices), while continuing to put emphasis on strengthening the basis for economic recovery," Matsushita said in a speech at a bankers' convention.
Matsushita said the current slowdown in Japan's economy is temporary and the chance that the recovery will continue is high.
"We are observing a drop in demand due to the effects of the increase in the sales tax. But the recovery trend of the overall economy remains intact with production and income holding firm," he said.
Japan's consumption tax was raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Given the steady improvement in employment and income, there is little chance that the recovery trend of private consumption in Japan will falter, Matsushita said.
He said that Japan's net exports are continuing to rise, while public investment is decreasing, and investment in housing is weak.
Production in the April-June period is likely to show a quarter-on-quarter drop, but the fall is expected to be minimal, he said.
He added that prices of goods are likely to remain stable for the time being, but the BOJ will continue to keep a careful watch over price movements.
